answer: No, the SIG did not settle on a new class structure. The topic ('New Issue: Non-human Actors', started by Robert Sanderson on 2021-09-21, using exactly the bird-building-a-nest example) was discussed through mid/late November 2021 but ended without agreement. Martin Doerr supported adding non-human (specifically living, biological) actors in principle, suggesting they belong in CRMsci as a sibling generalization to human actors, but insisted the SIG first needed real documented use-case data tracing individuals and domain (biology) experts before committing to new classes - he stated the reason animal actors were never modeled was precisely the lack of an experts group to consult. George Bruseker and Robert Sanderson produced a concrete draft class sketch (a new top class 'Agent' generalizing E39 Actor and a new sibling 'Biological Agent' branch, with parallel Individual Agent/Collective Agent and Individual Biological Agent/Collective Biological Agent classes, and renaming E39/E21/E74 to 'Human Agent'/'Human Person' accordingly), but this was only a discussion proposal, not adopted. Left unresolved: (1) whether/how to formally define 'individuality' and 'collectivity' for animals across the animal kingdom, (2) whether machines/robots/software should be treated similarly (Martin argued machines are not actors, just reactive instruments akin to traps, a separate modeling problem), (3) the cost/benefit and recall-precision methodological questions Martin posed about whether 'P12 occurred in the presence of' plus text is already sufficient versus needing new 'done by'-type properties/classes, and (4) finding biology/natural-history domain experts to validate the model. The thread's last message (2021-11-19) is just Martin sharing a background PowerPoint example of CRM-compatible animal tracking 'for future discussion' - no decision was recorded.
